known_callers.context: periodic creation controlled by fighter byte 0xf9

known_callers.source: one of the two fighter records selected by script data

original.discovery_notes: All three known callers first call 0x880053f4, proving that the destination is a cleared secondary-object record. The routine assigns its type byte and seeds words 0x04, 0x08, and 0x0c from a fighter record. copy_record_fields remains conservative because the exact meanings of those words are not fully verified.

commands: flatpak run org.mamedev.MAME kinst -rompath assets/ki1 -debug -nodrc -debugscript mame/oracle_ki15d_8800700c.cmd -video none -sound none -nothrottle -skip_gameinfo -seconds_to_run 3 -cfg_directory work/mame/cfg -diff_directory work/mame/diff
verification.notes: Three controlled calls were executed by the original R4600 instructions in MAME. The native test reproduces each output, confirms the 16-byte source is unchanged, and compares the full 1 MiB mapped test RAM byte-for-byte to prove that no unexpected location was modified. A separate live match trace reached the 0x88002bb4 caller organically after only its byte-0xf9 timer was armed: Jago's record at 0x8808bc00 seeded type 0x1f at 0x8808be00. The object retained Jago's copied words and owner byte for eight subsequent samples.
